2. The accused/applicants seek anticipatory bail in case FIR No. 0067/2025 of PS Crime Branch,
R.K. Puram, Delhi for offence under Section 420/406/34 IPC.
3. After part arguments, it appears that the IO has neither briefed the learned prosecutor nor he is aware about the complete facts of the case.

4. Broadly speaking, the prosecution case is as follows.

The accused/applicants took loan on few occasions from complainant Abhishek and even returned some of the loan but thereafter, the accused/applicants became dishonest and did not pay back the balance loan and since the repayment cheque got bounced, proceedings under Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act were initiated.
Further, the complainant Abhishek also introduced the accused/applicants with the other complainant Saurabh.

The accused/applicants took delivery of dry fruits from Saurabh as a business transaction but the cheques of payment issued by the accused/applicants got bounced, so proceedings under Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act are pending.
5. In response to a specific query, it is informed by the IO that the first cheque towards repayment of loan bounced on 02.04.2024 and that the loan was taken on 02.02.2023.
It is also informed by the IO that the alleged loan transactions were not in two instalments of Rs.50,00,000/- and Rs.55,00,000/- as mentioned in the FIR but in multiple instalments.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 06/01/2026 at 20:34:32 6.

Further, according to the accused/applicants, as against the loan amount of Rs.1,10,00,000/-,
they have already paid back almost Rs.2,00,00,000/- but that aspect has not been investigated.

In response, the IO submits that he had investigated the same and the complainants explained that the said amount was towards business of dairy products, though that business is nowhere disclosed in the FIR, which is otherwise a detailed one.
IO needs time to produce statements of the complainants in this regard.
7. Relist on 04.02.2026 in Advance List.
Interim orders to continue till next date of hearing.
GIRISH KATHPALIA, J JANUARY 6, 2026/
